title: Search a 2D Matrix
description: Treat the m x n matrix as one sorted array and binary search by mapping a flat index to row and column.

data.text: Given an `m x n` matrix where each row is sorted left-to-right and each column is sorted top-to-bottom (every element is greater than the one above and to its left), determine whether a target value exists. Must run in `O(m + n)` or better — here `O(log(mn))`.

Because the matrix is globally sorted, treat it as one contiguous sorted array of length `m*n`. A flat index `k` maps to `row = k / n`, `col = k % n`. Binary search over `[0, m*n)` takes `O(log(mn))` time and `O(1)` space.

data.title: Flattened binary search O(log mn)

data.text: Start at the top-right corner. If it equals the target, return true. If it is greater, the whole column below is larger, so move left. If it is smaller, the whole row to the left is smaller, so move down. Each step eliminates a full row or column — `O(m + n)` time, `O(1)` space, and it works even without the strict per-row sorted guarantee.

data.title: Staircase O(m + n)

data.caption: Staircase search from the top-right corner: move left to discard larger values, move down to discard smaller values, one full row or column per step.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[top-right: 7 > target=3] --> B[move left to 5]
    B --> C[5 > 3, move left to 3]
    C --> D[3 == 3: found!]
    style D fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: What improved?
data.text: A naive scan is O(mn). Flattening turns it into one sorted array for O(log(mn)). The staircase needs no sorted-column guarantee and runs in O(m + n). Use flatten when the matrix is strictly globally sorted; staircase when only row/column ordering holds.
